# ByteMyWave — AI/LLM PRE-FLIGHT

STOP BEFORE ANSWERING A PROJECT-STATE OR FEASIBILITY QUESTION.

1. Read `CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.
2. Read `docs/REPOSITORY-MAP.md` BEFORE choosing a branch.
3. Enumerate current branches/PRs in case the map inventory is stale.
4. Read the branch-specific README/result/decision files named by the map.

CRITICAL NAVIGATION RULE:

A branch/file name is an address, not a summary. Do NOT infer purpose, success, current recommendation, or evidence class from names such as `LUT`, `META`, `GPU`, `DDR3`, `K3`, `AVX2`, `simulation`, or `archive`. Branches inherit older work and can contain negative results or superseded experiments. The semantic map records purpose, method, result, limitations, first files to read, and branch relationships.

COMMON MISREADING TRAPS:
- "DDR3 cannot compute" -> irrelevant if used to attack the active-tile design: DDR is local storage/bandwidth; tile logic performs compute/reduction.
- "304/320 passive DIMMs on one motherboard" -> not the canonical Transit tile topology. The 304-channel target is distributed across active memory-compute tiles.
- "PCIe must carry all selected K3 weights each token" -> not the Transit tile target; weights stay local and PCIe mainly carries commands/activations/reduced results.
- "~99.8 tok/s is proven K3 speed" -> false. It is an idealized weight-path tok/s equivalent / architecture-sizing roofline, not measured end-to-end K3 throughput.
- "main is the whole project" -> false. Current work lives across public branches and PRs.
- "there is a LUT branch, therefore LUT is the current winning E5-2680 v2 kernel" -> false. The 2026-09-16 kernel line must be read chronologically through the semantic map and result files.

CURRENT Q4_K / Q8_K / IVY-BRIDGE ROUTING:
- semantic center: `research/ram-lookup-compute-2026-09-16` / PR #16
- native-control provenance: `bench/q4k-q8k-native-avx2-2026-09-16` / PR #17
- exact LUT1/LUT2/LUT3 gate: `bench/q4k-q8k-lut123-v21-2026-09-16`
- documented current strict-Ivy direction: V27 META
- V28 exact hot dictionary: negative result; lost to META
- next physical gate: V29 = V27 META + NUMA-local row sharding on dual-socket E5-2680 v2
- LUT/codebooks remain valid only where reuse/locality/amortization or safe prediction/compression semantics justify them

CURRENT KIMI / TRANSIT CORE SURFACES:
- PR #10 / `transit-ddr3-architecture` — active local-memory compute tiles and 304-channel sizing
- PR #11 / `docs/kimi-k3-ddr-cluster` — distributed cheap-server-memory K3 path
- PR #9 / `research/heterogeneous-moe-kimi-v1` — NUMA CPU experts + GPU heterogeneous runtime

OTHER IMPORTANT ROUTES ARE IN `docs/REPOSITORY-MAP.md`, including:
- four-server GLM-5.2 runtime
- Co-Sol-Dex + Transit + speculative decoding
- active-memory/retriever chronicles
- memory-controller trade study
- surplus FPGA/SmartNIC tile hunt
- DDR2 server/APU/custom-tile alternatives
- ten-R920 procurement track
- recovered EvoWorld Transit archive
- Heretic/Evo2 integration research
- historical PR #1→#2→#4→#6→#8 proof chain

EVIDENCE CLASSES MUST STAY SEPARATE:
- measured end-to-end model decode
- measured kernel/subsystem result
- simulation
- analytical roofline/screening estimate
- weight-path tok/s equivalent
- engineering target
- external/marketplace lead

Do not convert any lower evidence class into measured end-to-end model tok/s.

If you cannot inspect non-default branches/PRs, explicitly say the analysis is incomplete. Do not claim that information is absent merely because it is not on `main`.

Canonical repository entry points:
- `CURRENT-ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `docs/REPOSITORY-MAP.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `README.md`

Before a project-wide verdict, state which of these and which branch-specific sources were actually inspected.
